what_it_does: Quantum computers require frequent tuning (calibration) — adjusting the precise microwave pulses used to flip qubits — because each qubit pair behaves slightly differently and drifts over time. Current calibration routines treat all qubit pairs the same and run them one after another, which becomes a massive time sink as machines grow toward hundreds of qubits. This paper presents a two-step protocol: first, a quick profiling pass measures how each qubit pair responds to different pulse shapes and assigns each pair an appropriate calibration strategy from a small menu (rather than applying one-size-fits-all settings); second, a graph-based scheduling algorithm figures out which pairs can be calibrated simultaneously without interfering with each other, converting the serial schedule into a parallel one. The approach was tested on real IBM quantum hardware with up to 127 qubits.
